title: INNER JOIN
description: Learn how to use the INNER JOIN clause to query data from two or more related tables based on matching values.

data.alt: SQL Server Inner Join clause - select from three tables example
SQL Server Inner Join Sample Table

data.text: The inner join is one of the most commonly used joins in SQL Server. The INNER JOIN clause allows you to query data from two or more related tables.

Consider the products and categories tables. The products table contains a list of products with category IDs, but it does not show the category names. To include the category names in the result set, you use the INNER JOIN clause.

data.title: Query Products Without Category Names
data.content: Products table shows category_id, not category_name.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price,
    category_id
FROM
    production.products
ORDER BY
    product_name DESC;

data.title: INNER JOIN to Include Category Names
data.content: Join products with categories to show category_name.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    category_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products p
INNER JOIN production.categories c
    ON c.category_id = p.category_id
ORDER BY
    product_name DESC;

data.text: In this query, c and p are table aliases for the production.categories and production.products tables. By using aliases, you can reference columns as alias.column_name instead of using the full table_name.column_name, saving typing.

For each row in the products table, the INNER JOIN clause matches it with every row in the categories table based on the values of the category_id column. If both rows have the same category_id, a new row is formed and included in the result set. If a product row has no matching category, it is ignored.

data.title: INNER JOIN Syntax
data.content: Join two tables where the join predicate is TRUE.
data.code:
SELECT
    select_list
FROM
    T1
INNER JOIN T2 ON join_predicate;

items: Specify the main table (T1) in the FROM clause.
Specify the second table in the INNER JOIN clause (T2) and a join predicate.
Only rows that cause the join predicate to evaluate to TRUE are included in the result set.

data.text: The INNER JOIN clause compares each row of table T1 with rows of table T2 to find all pairs of rows that satisfy the join predicate. If the predicate evaluates to TRUE, the column values of the matching rows of T1 and T2 are combined into a new row and included in the result set.
Note that the INNER keyword is optional. You can use JOIN instead of INNER JOIN:

data.title: JOIN Without INNER Keyword
data.content: INNER is optional; JOIN alone implies INNER JOIN.
data.code:
SELECT
    select_list
FROM
    T1
JOIN T2 ON join_predicate;

data.text: You can use multiple INNER JOIN clauses to query data from three or more tables. For example, to include brand information alongside product and category data.

data.title: Joining Three Tables
data.content: Join products, categories, and brands in a single query.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    category_name,
    brand_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products p
INNER JOIN production.categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
INNER JOIN production.brands b ON b.brand_id = p.brand_id
ORDER BY
    product_name DESC;

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Use table aliases when joining multiple tables to make queries shorter and easier to read. The alias must be used to refer to the table columns throughout the query.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: INNER JOIN returns only matching rows from both tables.
Use the ON clause to specify the join condition.
The INNER keyword is optional; JOIN alone implies INNER JOIN.
You can chain multiple INNER JOIN clauses for three or more tables.
Table aliases make join queries more readable and shorter.
